title: Chance and glide
learned: A random module gives a new voltage on every clock: through a quantizer, a melody nobody wrote
LEVEL sets the range of the random voltages: how wide the melody jumps
A slew limiter slows a voltage down: on pitch it makes notes glide

steps.why: Instead of writing a melody, you can let chance write it and keep only the scale. Random voltages, quantized, give endless melodies that always fit.
steps.do: The quantized melody plays. In the rack there is a random module (JX-RND) and a slew limiter (JX-SLW). Press Next.

steps.why: The random module picks a new value on every clock pulse.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from X2 of the clock to CLOCK of the random module (X2 already feeds the sequencer).
steps.after: It now draws a new random voltage on every eighth note, in step with the sequencer.

steps.why: STEP holds each random value until the next pulse: a staircase of random notes.
steps.do: Drag a cable from STEP of the random module to the V/OCT input of the quantizer (it replaces the sequencer's CV).
steps.after: A melody nobody wrote, always in the scale. The sequencer still plays the gates, so its rests and rhythm stay; only the pitches are random now.

steps.why: LEVEL sets how wide the random voltages spread, and so how far the melody jumps.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn LEVEL of the random module down and up.
steps.after: Low, the melody stays within a few notes; high, it leaps over octaves. At full level the random voltage spans ±5 V: ten octaves, mostly too much.

steps.why: A slew limiter lets a voltage change only so fast. On pitch, the note slides to the next one instead of jumping: glide, or portamento.
steps.do: Press F2. Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from the V/OCT output of the quantizer to IN of the slew limiter, then drag OUT of the slew limiter to V/OCT of the oscillator (it replaces the cable from the quantizer).
steps.after: No change yet: RISE and FALL are at zero, so the voltage passes at full speed.

steps.why: RISE is how slowly the voltage may go up, FALL how slowly it may go down.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn RISE and FALL of the slew limiter up a little.
steps.after: The notes now slide into each other, like a singer or a trombone. With only RISE turned up, the notes glide up and jump down. The same module smooths any jumpy voltage, not only pitch.

steps.do: Chance writes the notes, the quantizer keeps them in key, the slew makes them sing. Press Next to finish.
